title: Reading Charts
promise: Candles are the language of price: a diary of fear and greed.
unlock: Read any candle: open, high, low and close
Spot the hammer, the doji and the engulfing candle
Zoom out first, and trade the timeframe that matches your hold
Tell a believable breakout from a weak one with volume
Find support and resistance, and place your stop beyond them

questions.q: This red candle opened at $50. Where did it close?

items.label: A red candle: body from $50 down to $47, wicks up to $52 and down to $46

options: $50: red means it closed at the open
questions.why: A red body runs from the open at the top down to the close at the bottom: $47. The wick below reaches the low, $46.
questions.work: Open $50 − close $47 = $3 lower: a red candle.

questions.q: After a 10-day rise, today brings a doji at $80. What does it say?

chart.label: Ten rising days, then a doji at $80

options: Sell now: the rise is over
Indecision: a clue to watch, not a signal
questions.why: A doji shows a draw between buyers and sellers. After a long rise it’s a clue to watch, never a sell signal on its own.
questions.work: Open $80, close $80: nobody won the day. Wait for the next candles.

questions.q: You’ll hold for weeks. The daily chart is in an uptrend, but the 15-minute chart is dipping. Which should you trust?

chart.label: Daily candles rising over three months

options: The daily chart: it matches your hold
Neither: you wait until both agree
questions.why: Trade from the chart that matches your hold. For weeks that’s the daily, and it’s rising. A 15-minute dip is noise inside it.

questions.q: A stock breaks above $40 on 500,000 shares. It usually trades 1,000,000 a day. How believable is the breakout?

chart.label: Price breaks above $40 on half the average volume

options: Very: the price broke out, that’s enough
Weak: half the usual crowd joined
Bearish: low volume means it will fall
questions.why: Few people backed this move, so it’s easier to reverse. Low volume shows a weak move, not which way price goes next.

questions.q: You buy at $62. Support sits at $60, where buyers stepped in twice before. Where is a sensible stop?

chart.label: Price bounces off $60 twice; you buy at $62

questions.why: Support is a zone, and price often pokes into it before turning. A stop on $60 or at $61.50 gets hit by normal noise; a little below the zone gives the trade room.

retry.q: This green candle opened at $30. Where did it close?

items.label: A green candle: body from $30 up to $33, wicks up to $34 and down to $29

retry.why: On a green candle the body runs up from the open to the close, so its top is the close. The wick above reaches the high, $34.
retry.work: Close $33 − open $30 = $3 higher: a green candle.
retry.added: Retry set written for the Academy

retry.q: After a 6-day fall, a candle opens at $25 and closes at $25, with wicks on both sides. What does it say?

chart.label: Six falling days, then a doji at $25

options: Indecision: a clue to watch, not a signal
retry.why: Open and close at the same price: neither side won the day. After a fall it’s a clue to watch. Wait for the next candles before you act.
retry.added: Retry set written for the Academy

retry.q: You’ll hold for a few hours. The hourly chart is rising, but the 1-minute chart just dipped. Which chart do you trade from?
options: The hourly: it matches your hold
The monthly: longer is always right
retry.why: Match the chart to your hold: hours means the hourly, with a look at the daily first. A 1-minute dip is noise, and a monthly candle is longer than your whole trade.
retry.added: Retry set written for the Academy

retry.q: A stock breaks above $25 on 2,400,000 shares. It usually trades 800,000 a day. How believable is the breakout?

chart.label: Price breaks above $25 on three times the average volume

options: Believable: three times the usual crowd joined
Bearish: high volume means it will fall
retry.why: Many more people than usual backed the move, so it’s harder to reverse. Volume shows how strong a move is, not which way it goes.
retry.added: Retry set written for the Academy

retry.q: You buy at $103. Support sits at $100, where buyers stepped in three times. Where is a sensible stop?

chart.label: Price bounces off $100 three times; you buy at $103

retry.why: Price often pokes into a support zone before it turns. A stop a little below the zone survives that noise; one on the line or just under your entry doesn’t.
retry.added: Retry set written for the Academy

refresher.title: Lesson 1 · One candle, four prices
refresher.text: The body runs from open to close; the wicks reach the high and the low. Green: the close is the top of the body. Red: the close is the bottom.

refresher.title: Lesson 2 · Candles that tell a story
refresher.text: A doji means open ≈ close: indecision. One candle is a clue, never a signal on its own, and where it appears matters.

refresher.title: Lesson 3 · Timeframes: same stock, different story
refresher.text: Trade from the chart that matches your hold: hours → hourly, weeks → daily, months → weekly. Check one chart bigger first: it sets the trend.

refresher.title: Lesson 4 · Volume: the crowd behind the move
refresher.text: Volume = shares traded. A breakout on above-normal volume has more people behind it; one on half the usual volume is easier to reverse. Volume shows strength, not direction.

refresher.title: Lesson 5 · Support and resistance
refresher.text: Support is a zone, not a line. Put the stop a little beyond it, not on it. Support near $40? A stop around $38, not $40.
